Customer: Haan haan, dekh, abhi mera salary nahi aaya na. Kal ya parso aayega. Toh kal main call kar dunga.

Agent: Kal? Okay sir, kal kaunsa din hoga? Aaj toh Wednesday hai. Kal Thursday ko aap payment kar denge, theek hai?

Agent: Theek hai sir. Toh kal Thursday ko aap 52,300 rupees pay kar denge, haan? Aapka salary kal credit hoga?

Customer: <interruption> Haan, haan, bilkul. Kal hi. Aap tension mat lo.

Agent: Sir, ek minute. Aapka salary account kaunsa hai? Main aapko payment link bheju?

Agent: Sir, penalty charge toh late payment ke liye lagta hai. Aapne 18th ko payment nahi kiya, toh naturally penalty add hoga. Yeh sab theek hai.

Customer: Nahi nahi, yeh theek nahi hai. Aapne mujhe pehle bataya tha ki penalty sirf 2,000 hoga, lekin 4,500 ho gaya. Yeh galat hai. Pehle toh aap isko correct karo, phir main payment kar dunga.

Agent: Sir, main aapke liye statement check kar dunga. Lekin aap kal payment kar do, phir hum penalty ko dekh lenge, theek hai?

Customer: Nahi, pehle correct karo. Mujhe nahi pata ki aap sach bol rahe ho ya nahi. Mujhe proper statement bhejo, phir main soch lunga.

Agent: Sir, main aapko statement email kar dunga. Aap dekh lena. Lekin aap kal payment ka promise kar rahe ho, theek hai? Kal Thursday ko 52,300 rupees?

Customer: Haan haan, kal. Kal hi. Lekin statement pehle bhej do. Aur ek aur baat — mera ek aur loan bhi hai ICICI se, aur unhe bhi payment dena hai. Toh pehle unhe de dunga, phir tumhare ko.

Agent: Sir, aapka ICICI loan kab due hai?

Customer: Kal hi. Toh pehle unhe priority dunga. Aapko kal raat ko payment mil jayega, okay?

Agent: Sir, kal raat ko? Matlab aap kal pura din ICICI ko denge, aur raat ko hume?

Customer: Haan, haan, kuch aisa hi. Dekh, main abhi busy hoon. Mujhe ek meeting mein jana hai. Tum mujhe kal call kar lena, theek hai? Kal call kar lena.

Agent: Sir, ek minute. Aap kal kaunsa time available ho? Subah, dopahar, ya shaam?

Customer: Haan haan, shaam ko. Shaam ko call kar lena. Aur haan, statement bhejna na.

Agent: Theek hai sir. Toh kal shaam 6 baje main aapko call kar dunga. Aur aap kal payment kar denge, theek hai?

Customer: Haan, haan, bilkul. Kal. Bye.

Agent: Sir, wait. Aapka contact number toh theek hai na? Yeh wala number?

Customer: Haan, yeh wala theek hai. Okay, bye.

Agent: Theek hai sir. Kal shaam ko. Thank you.

transcript:
Agent: Hello, am I speaking with Vikram Sharma?

Customer: Haan, haan, this is Vikram. Kaun bol raha hai?

Agent: Hi Vikram, this is Deepak from Fintech Collections. I'm calling about your loan account ending in 7834. You have an outstanding EMI of 22,500 rupees that was due on the 18th. It's now the 24th, so we're looking at a six-day overdue situation. Do you have a few minutes?

Customer: Bilkul, bilkul, I know about this. Actually, yaar, I tried to pay it already. Two days back I attempted through Google Pay, but the transaction failed. The money was deducted from my HDFC account, but it never reached your system. Dekho, I'm really stressed about this.

Agent: Okay, I understand. That's a gateway issue then. Let me check our records... I'm not seeing any payment received on your account as of today. Can you tell me exactly what happened when you tried to pay?

Customer: I opened Google Pay, entered your payment link, amount 22,500 rupees. I pressed confirm, and it showed loading for maybe thirty seconds, then suddenly it said "Transaction Failed — Please Try Again." But when I checked my balance, the money was already gone from my account. It's been two days and the money is still stuck.

Agent: Okay, so the funds were debited but the payment didn't come through to us. This sounds like a UPI gateway timeout or a network issue on the payment processor's end. Did you receive any reference number or transaction ID from Google Pay?

Customer: Haan, yes, I have it. UPI Ref: 334521789. The timestamp shows 22nd June, 3:15 PM. Should I try paying again right now? I'm really worried, yaar.

Agent: Before you do that, let me advise you. Since the first attempt failed at the gateway level, if you try the same UPI link immediately, there's a risk of a duplicate debit. The funds from your first attempt should be reversed by HDFC within 24 to 48 hours. In the meantime, I can offer you an alternate payment method that might be more reliable.

Customer: What are the options? I really want to clear this. My credit score is already affected, and I don't want this to go further. Bilkul, I want to pay.

Agent: Good, I appreciate your willingness. Here are your options: First, you can attempt a direct NEFT transfer to our bank account. Second, you can visit any HDFC branch and deposit the amount in cash directly to our collection account. Or third, we can set up an auto-debit from your account for tomorrow morning, which would bypass the UPI layer entirely.

Customer: <interruption> The NEFT option — how long does that take? I'm worried about the timing. I'm at work in Noida right now, so branch deposit is not possible today. And auto-debit, dekho, last month my auto-debit failed due to insufficient balance and I got charged a bounce fee. I don't want that to happen again.

Agent: NEFT typically takes two to four hours during business hours. If you initiate it before 3 PM, it should be credited by end of business today. However, it's already 4:30 PM, so if you do it now, it might process tomorrow morning. The branch deposit would be immediate, but you'd need to visit in person. The auto-debit would be the safest option, but I understand your concern given last month's experience.

Customer: Okay, okay, so NEFT would be the best option then. Can you give me the details? I'll do it right now from my office computer.

Agent: Perfect. The details are: Account Name — Fintech Collections Pvt Ltd, Account Number — 5012456789, IFSC Code — HDFC0001234. The amount is 22,500 rupees. Can you confirm you have these details?

Customer: Yes, I'm writing them down. HDFC0001234, account number 5012456789, Fintech Collections. Amount 22,500. I'll do this right now.

Agent: Once you initiate the NEFT, you should receive a confirmation message from HDFC with a transaction reference number. Please save that and share it with me so I can track it on our end. What time do you expect to complete this?

Customer: I'm doing it right now. Let me log into net banking... okay, I'm in. I'm entering the beneficiary details... amount 22,500... <interruption> wait, it's asking me to confirm the beneficiary name. It shows "Fintech Collections Pvt Ltd" — is that correct?

Agent: Yes, that's correct. Go ahead and confirm.

Customer: Okay, confirmed. Now it's asking for my OTP. I should receive an SMS in a moment... yes, I got it. Entering the OTP now... and... submitted. It says "NEFT Transfer Initiated Successfully." The reference number is NEFT2024062400921. The timestamp is 4:32 PM.

Agent: Excellent, Vikram. That's great news. Please note down that reference number — NEFT2024062400921. The funds should be credited to our account by tomorrow morning, latest by 11 AM. Once it's credited, your account will be updated and the overdue status will be cleared. In the meantime, regarding the UPI payment that failed on the 22nd, you should contact HDFC customer care with that reference number — UPI Ref: 334521789 — and request a reversal. They typically process reversals within 48 hours.

Customer: Okay, I'll do that. So my account will be clear once this NEFT goes through?

Agent: Yes, once the 22,500 rupees is credited, your outstanding amount will be zero and the overdue status will be removed. However, I do want to mention that since you were six days overdue, there may be a late payment fee of around 400 rupees that will be added to your account. But that's separate from the EMI itself. Your next EMI of 22,500 is due on the 18th of next month. Can I confirm your contact number is still 9876543210?

Customer: Yes, that's correct. And just to confirm — once I pay this NEFT, I don't need to do anything else, right? The account will be updated automatically?

Agent: Correct. Our system will match the NEFT reference number with your account and update it automatically once the funds are received. I'll also make a note on your account that you've initiated the NEFT today, so if there's any delay, we can investigate using the reference number. You should receive an SMS confirmation from us once the payment is credited. Is there anything else I can help you with today?

Customer: No, I think that's it. Thank you for helping me sort this out, yaar. I was really stressed about the UPI failure.

Agent: You're welcome, Vikram. I'm glad we could find a solution. Just remember to follow up with HDFC about the failed UPI reversal, and keep that NEFT reference number safe. We'll be in touch once the payment is credited. Have a good day.

Customer: Thank you. Bye.

transcript:
Agent: Hello, is this Rajesh Kumar?

Customer: Haan, yes, this is Rajesh speaking. Who is calling, please?

Agent: Hi Rajesh, this is Priya from Finserve Collections. I'm calling about your loan account, the one ending in 4521. You are having some time to talk, no?

Customer: Arre, I am bit busy right now, but okay, tell me what is the matter.

Agent: Sir, your account is showing overdue status now. Last payment you made was 15th September, and since that time we are not receiving anything. The outstanding balance is Rs. 1,84,500. Can we discuss what is happening?

Customer: <interruption> Yes, yes, I know about this. But look, I want to pay, okay? The thing is... things have become very difficult for me right now. Very difficult.

Agent: I understand, sir. Can you tell me what the situation is exactly? What is the challenge you are facing?

Customer: Actually, I lost my job, Priya. I was working as senior accountant in one manufacturing company in Pune, and two months back, the company did restructuring. They removed almost entire finance department. I was one of them also.

Agent: Oh, I see. So you are currently without job, is it?

Customer: Yes, exactly. I am searching for work, but the market is very tough, no? It is not easy to find good position so quickly. My wife, she is teacher, but her salary alone... it is not sufficient. We have two children in school, and there are other loans also. The expenses are too much.

Agent: I understand. So you have other loan obligations as well?

Customer: Yes, home loan from another bank, and personal loan from my previous company credit union. Combined EMI is around Rs. 35,000 per month. My wife's salary is Rs. 42,000 only, and after tax and other expenses, nothing is left. That is why I cannot pay your EMI.

Agent: Rajesh, this is difficult situation, I can see. Tell me, do you have any savings or other income source right now?

Customer: No, nothing. I am using my savings for basic expenses, but that is running out now. I applied to maybe 15-20 companies, but nothing came through. I am hoping something will come in next month or two, but I cannot promise anything right now.

Agent: I appreciate your honesty, sir. Given this situation, we need to assess your case properly. This is what we call hardship case. Before we can discuss options like extending tenure or reducing EMI temporarily, I need to confirm — do you have any document showing your job loss? Termination letter or severance notice?

Customer: Yes, I have the termination letter. They gave it in writing. I can send it to you if you need.

Agent: That would be very helpful. Can you email it to our hardship team? I will give you the email address. Now, because you are facing genuine income disruption due to job loss, we can escalate your case for hardship assessment. This might lead to options like temporary moratorium on payments, or restructured EMI that is lower than current amount.

Customer: <interruption> Moratorium means I don't have to pay for some time, is it?

Agent: Exactly, sir. Moratorium is temporary pause on payments, usually 3 to 6 months, depending on policy and your situation. But this is not automatic — it requires approval from management team. They will review your case, your income documents, your employment situation.

Customer: Okay, that sounds good. But how much time will this take?

Agent: Assessment usually takes 5 to 7 working days once we receive all documents. So if you send termination letter and your wife's salary slip, we can move forward quickly.

Customer: Alright, I can do that. But I want to be honest — even if you give moratorium, I am still worried what happens after. If I don't find job by then, what happens to me?

Agent: That is fair concern, Rajesh. If you don't find employment by end of moratorium period, we can reassess and potentially extend it or look at other options like tenure extension. But first step is to get your hardship case formally assessed. Without that, I cannot offer any relief.

Customer: Okay, I understand. So what should I do now?

Agent: Here is what I need from you: First, send termination letter and your wife's latest salary slip to hardship@finserve.com. Second, don't make any payment on this account until we complete assessment — making payment might complicate the hardship review. Third, I will schedule follow-up call with you in 7 days to check status of documents and assessment.

Customer: Alright, I will send documents tomorrow. And you will call me back in one week?

Agent: Yes, sir. I will personally ensure you get call within 7 days. In the meantime, if situation changes — for example, if you find employment — please reach out to us immediately. That will also help speed up the process.

Customer: Thank you. I was really worried you will just keep calling and demanding payment without understanding what is happening.

Agent: Not at all, Rajesh. We understand that job loss is genuine hardship, and we are here to work with you, not against you. Let me confirm details one more time: your email is rajesh.kumar.1985@gmail.com, correct?

Customer: Yes, that is correct.

Agent: Perfect. I have logged your case as hardship assessment due to job loss and income disruption. You will hear from us within 7 days. Please do send those documents as soon as possible.

Customer: Thank you. I will. Goodbye.

Agent: Goodbye, Rajesh.
